claim: With alignment and every other rule at zero, directional agreement never moves from its starting value.
derivation: This is the brief's example 'alignment weight 0 ⇒ directional agreement stays low', in the form the equations settle exactly.
With alignment and every other weight at 0 and no beacons or obstacles, each steering term is 0 · (finite vector) = 0 (E3–E7), so a = 0 (E8).
Then v′ = v + 0 · Δt = v exactly, and the speed clamp leaves the starting speed 2.7 alone because it lies in [0.45, 3.6] (E9, E15).
Headings never change, so directionalAgreement equals its starting value bit for bit at every step (E12). flock.rules-off.initial-agreement-low shows that starting value is low.

Why only this form: with separation and cohesion on, attraction and repulsion alone can align some flocks, so 'stays low' is not derivable there; flock.no-alignment.stays-disordered records that case as an expected-qualitative check.
